subject: Redwood vs Hyperscaler latency/throughput benchmarks \u2014 post-call recap & next tests
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: David Reynolds <d.reynolds@globex.com>, Ava Turner <ava.turner@globex.com>, Jason Li <j.li@globex.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood vs Hyperscaler latency/throughput benchmarks — post-call recap & next tests

Hi David / Ava / Jason —

Thanks again for the call earlier — really appreciate the clear framing on your 1) latency SLOs for interactive calls (p95 <= 120ms target) and 2) high-throughput batch inference (tokens/sec & cost tradeoffs). Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have the same plan: 

What we agreed:
- Run a 48-hour A/B test: Redwood hosted Dedicated pool (config A) vs your hyperscaler baseline (config B).
- Test workload: 500k requests (mixed chat prompts + completion), 80/20 short/long token distribution.
- Metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99 latencies, median tokens/sec, sustained tokens/sec, error rate, cost per 1M tokens.
- Models: open-model variant (quantized) + full fp16 baseline on both sides.

Actions / asks from Globex:
1) Share a read-only AWS role (or test account) to run the hyperscaler-side harness, or confirm you want us to run both sides from Redwood and you’ll accept the results.
2) Provide a small sample of the request distribution (anonymized) so we can mirror it in the harness.
3) Confirm the test window (we proposed Tue–Thu next week).

We attached the A/B test plan (redwood_globex_abtest_plan_v3.pdf) and a short slide deck with the measurement approach. We’ll also generate an output CSV with p95/p99 and tokens/sec once the run completes.

Next meeting: propose a 30-min review on Thu following the test — move to calendar once dates confirmed.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate with Rafael and Vivek on the test harness.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
(415) 555-0132

From: David Reynolds <d.reynolds@globex.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Ava Turner <ava.turner@globex.com>, Jason Li <j.li@globex.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood vs Hyperscaler latency/throughput benchmarks — post-call recap & next tests

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. We’re aligned on the test goals. A couple quick clarifications before we hand over the role: 

- For p95/p99: are you using observed end-to-end latency (client request to first token) or server-side node latency? We prefer end-to-end numbers that include network overhead.
- For models: can you confirm the exact versions you’ll run for the hyperscaler baseline? Our infra team will want to mirror runtime flags.

We can provide a temporary cross-account role for your test harness. I’ll ask infra to spin that up and share the ARN by Monday. We can confirm Tue–Thu for the run window.

Also, please confirm if Redwood will run the hyperscaler-side tests in our account (preferred) or if you need us to run them and hand over logs.

Appreciate it — look forward to the results.

-David
David Reynolds
Head of AI Engineering, Globex Corporation
d.reynolds@globex.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 10:20:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Redwood vs Hyperscaler latency/throughput benchmarks — internal next steps

Rafael / Vivek — forwarding the thread with Globex. They’ll provide a cross-account role (ARN) early next week. Key ask: please prepare the harness to run two configurations in-parallel:

Config A (Redwood Dedicated):
- Instance pool: rtx-a100-equivalent cluster (our Dedicated pool)
- Model: open-model-v1-quant (INT8-friendly) and open-model-v1-fp16 baseline
- Runtime flags: continuous batching disabled for latency run; enabled for throughput run

Config B (Globex hyperscaler baseline):
- We’ll run in their AWS account; Rafael to coordinate role and infra setup with their infra team (David).

Measurement details:
- Latency: capture end-to-end time from client to first token and last token; compute p50/p95/p99.
- Throughput: tokens/sec measured at max sustainable QPS for 10-minute windows; report median and 95th percentile tokens/sec across windows.

Deliverables (post-run):
- redwood_globex_abtest_results_v2.csv (raw per-request log aggregated)
- Redwood vs Hyperscaler slides (summary)
- Link to Grafana dashboard & raw logs

Note: keep experiment flags identical across runs (batch sizes, sequence lengths, concurrency). Rafael — can you confirm you can run the hyperscaler-side harness in their account, and if you need an infra handoff? Also add any stabilization steps (warmup policy) you think necessary.

Thanks — I’ll follow up once Globex shares the ARN.

-Marissa

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: David Reynolds <d.reynolds@globex.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Feb 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood vs Hyperscaler latency/throughput benchmarks — results & next steps

Hi David / Ava / Jason —

We completed the 48-hour A/B run (runs executed: 2027-02-24 00:00 UTC — 2027-02-26 23:59 UTC). Attached is a quick summary and the raw CSV (redwood_globex_abtest_results_v2.csv). High-level results below (Redwood Dedicated vs Globex hyperscaler baseline):

Summary (median over test windows):
- Latency (end-to-end, first token):
  - Redwood Dedicated: p50=34ms, p95=82ms, p99=147ms
  - Globex baseline: p50=45ms, p95=130ms, p99=260ms
- Throughput (tokens/sec, sustained):
  - Redwood Dedicated: median=12.5k tokens/sec, 95th=13.2k
  - Globex baseline: median=9.1k tokens/sec, 95th=9.7k
- Error rate: Redwood 0.2% | Globex 0.6%
- Cost per 1M tokens (approx): Redwood $28 | Globex $36

Notes:
- We ran two modes: latency-focused (batching off) and throughput-focused (batching on). The numbers above are the best-of for each target metric. Full per-run breakdown is in the CSV.
- The hyperscaler run included identical model weights and runtime flags to the extent supported by their environment; minor infra variance captured in logs.

Next steps:
1) Marissa — propose a 30-min review early next week to walk through the CSV and Grafana dashboards.
2) We can run a follow-up with more load shapes (longer sequences / heavier tail) if Globex wants deeper tail analysis.
3) If results look good, we can draft a pilot agreement for Redwood Dedicated capacity (proposal to include SLA targets and expected unit pricing).

Links / artifacts:
- Results CSV: attached (redwood_globex_abtest_results_v2.csv)
- Summary slides: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c-redwood-abtest-plan
- Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/abcd123/globex-abtest

Happy to hop on a call to walk through any of the numbers.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.com
